name: Valpolicella
summary: A Veneto red wine zone in the hills north of Verona, with vineyards on largely calcareous soils. Styles run from fresh, light reds with high acidity to Amarone, made from partly dried grapes.
pairing: Simple Valpolicella suits burgers and roast or grilled chicken.
label_note: Classico: only from the historic zone of Negrar, Marano, Fumane, Sant'Ambrogio and San Pietro in Cariano. Valpantena: from that valley. Superiore: at least one year of ageing from 1 January after the harvest. Amarone needs at least two years, and four for Riserva.

grapes.name: Corvina
grapes.local_note: With Corvinone it makes up 45 to 95 percent of the blend; Rondinella adds 5 to 30 percent.

appellations.name: Valpolicella
appellations.note: DOC; may add Classico, Valpantena and Superiore.

appellations.name: Valpolicella Classico
appellations.note: The historic zone in Negrar, Marano, Fumane, Sant'Ambrogio and San Pietro in Cariano.

appellations.name: Valpolicella Valpantena
appellations.note: Geographic mention for the Valpantena valley.

appellations.name: Valpolicella Ripasso
appellations.note: DOC over the same comuni; may add Superiore.

appellations.name: Amarone della Valpolicella
appellations.note: DOCG from dried grapes; also Classico, Valpantena and Riserva.

appellations.name: Recioto della Valpolicella
appellations.note: Sweet DOCG from dried grapes, also as spumante.

name: Soave
summary: Hills east of Verona where volcanic basalt and limestone soils meet. Garganega gives dry, crisp whites with good acidity, often with an almond note on the finish.
pairing: Soave suits fish, from lighter fish dishes to tuna sashimi.
label_note: Classico: only from the historic zone in part of Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, recognised in 1931. Colli Scaligeri is a hill sub zone. Soave Superiore and Recioto di Soave are separate DOCGs.

grapes.name: Garganega
grapes.local_note: At least 70 percent of the blend, with Trebbiano di Soave and Chardonnay up to 30 percent.

appellations.name: Soave
appellations.note: DOC, still and spumante.

appellations.name: Soave Classico
appellations.note: The historic hill zone between Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone.

appellations.name: Soave Colli Scaligeri
appellations.note: Sub zone with its own delimited area.

appellations.name: Soave Superiore
appellations.note: DOCG over the same hills, also Classico and Riserva.

appellations.name: Recioto di Soave
appellations.note: Sweet DOCG from dried grapes, mainly Garganega; also Classico and spumante.

name: Prosecco
summary: Prosecco DOC spans nine provinces across Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia in northeast Italy. Made mainly from Glera, with the second fermentation in tank, the wines are fruity, with green apple and pear notes.
pairing: Prosecco suits Italian cured meats and spicy noodle dishes.
label_note: Made as Prosecco, Prosecco spumante, spumante rosé and frizzante. "Treviso" or "Trieste" may appear when all grapes come from, and the wine is made and bottled in, that province.

grapes.name: Glera
grapes.local_note: At least 85 percent of the blend.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: Required at 10 to 15 percent in Prosecco Rosé.

appellations.name: Prosecco
appellations.note: DOC over nine provinces of Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia.

appellations.name: Prosecco Rosé
appellations.note: Spumante rosé from Glera with Pinot Nero.

appellations.name: Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco
appellations.note: Separate DOCG in the province of Treviso.

appellations.name: Asolo Prosecco
appellations.note: Separate DOCG in the province of Treviso.

name: Alto Adige
summary: Alpine valleys in Italy's far north, with vineyards from warm low sites around Bolzano to cool high slopes. About two thirds of the wine is white, beside light Schiava and darker, firmer Lagrein reds.
label_note: The German "Südtirol" or "Südtiroler" may be used. Riserva needs at least two years of ageing from 1 October of the harvest year. Six sub zones may be named on the label.

grapes.name: Pinot Gris
grapes.local_note: Pinot Grigio; the most planted variety.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: Pinot Nero, Blauburgunder; the most planted red.

grapes.name: Schiava
grapes.local_note: Vernatsch; once most of the vineyard area, now about eighth.

appellations.name: Alto Adige
appellations.note: DOC for the whole wine growing area of the province of Bolzano.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Colli di Bolzano
appellations.note: Sub zone, Bozner Leiten in German.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Meranese
appellations.note: Sub zone, Meraner in German.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Santa Maddalena
appellations.note: Sub zone, St. Magdalener in German.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Terlano
appellations.note: Sub zone, Terlaner in German.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Valle Isarco
appellations.note: Sub zone, Eisacktaler in German.

appellations.name: Alto Adige Valle Venosta
appellations.note: Sub zone, Vinschgau in German.

name: Friuli
summary: Hills and stony plains of Friuli Venezia Giulia, sheltered by the Alps to the north and tempered by the Adriatic. Most of its types are named after one grape, whites such as Friulano and Ribolla Gialla beside reds such as Merlot.
label_note: Varietal wines need at least 85 percent of the named grape. No type may use Riserva. The Slovenian names Furlanija and Furlanija Julijska krajina may be used.

appellations.name: Friuli
appellations.note: DOC across the comuni of the region listed in its text; also labelled Friuli Venezia Giulia.

appellations.name: Friuli Colli Orientali
appellations.note: DOC within the area, with sub zones such as Cialla and Ribolla Gialla di Rosazzo.

appellations.name: Colli Orientali del Friuli Picolit
appellations.note: DOCG for Picolit, amabile or dolce.

appellations.name: Friuli Grave
appellations.note: DOC within the area.

appellations.name: Friuli Isonzo
appellations.note: DOC within the area.

name: Etna
summary: Vineyards on the slopes of Mount Etna in Sicily, on volcanic soils. Reds from Nerello Mascalese are pale in colour and light in body, yet tannic.
label_note: Rosso Riserva needs at least four years of ageing, twelve months in wood. Bianco Superiore comes only from Milo. Spumante is bottle fermented with at least 18 months on the lees. A listed contrada may follow the name.

grapes.name: Nerello Mascalese
grapes.local_note: At least 80 percent of Etna Rosso and Rosato, with Nerello Cappuccio up to 20 percent.

grapes.name: Carricante
grapes.local_note: At least 60 percent of Etna Bianco and 80 percent of Bianco Superiore.

appellations.name: Etna Rosso
appellations.note: Also Riserva.

appellations.name: Etna Bianco
appellations.note: Bianco Superiore from Milo only.

appellations.name: Etna Spumante
appellations.note: White or rosé, mainly Nerello Mascalese.

name: Franciacorta
summary: Morainic hills just south of Lake Iseo, near Brescia in Lombardy. The sparkling wines get their second fermentation in the bottle and age at least 18 months on the lees.
pairing: Franciacorta suits cheese, including soft cheeses.
label_note: Minimum time on the lees: 18 months, 24 for Satèn and Rosé, 30 for Millesimato, 60 for Riserva, which must also show the vintage.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: Over three quarters of the vineyard area.

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: Pinot Nero; about 17 percent of the area, at least 35 percent of a rosé.

grapes.name: Pinot Blanc
grapes.local_note: Pinot Bianco; about 3 percent of the area, at most 50 percent of a blend.

appellations.name: Franciacorta
appellations.note: DOCG, bottle fermented.

appellations.name: Franciacorta Satèn
appellations.note: White grapes only.

name: Taurasi
summary: Hills of Irpinia in the province of Avellino, inland Campania, with volcanic soils in places. Taurasi is made mostly from Aglianico, a tannic red with high acidity that is built for long ageing.
label_note: At least three years of ageing, one in wood, before release. Riserva needs four years, eighteen months in wood.

appellations.name: Taurasi
appellations.note: DOCG in 17 comuni of Avellino province.
